author.description: My name is Patrik Bak. As a former three-time participant and two-time medalist at the International Mathematical Olympiads (IMO), but also the author of many competition problems (including two for the IMO), I have a deep relationship with Olympiad mathematics. I have long enjoyed combining mathematics with programming. This interest previously led to the GeoGen project, a tool for automatically generating geometric problems. MathComps is the next logical step on this path – an effort to create a comprehensive and modern platform for the mathematical olympiad community. In building it, I rely not only on my own knowledge and experience but also on feedback and ideas from many great people in the MO community.
author.title: About the author

story.text1: The world of mathematical competitions is vast, full of problems, sources, and materials. However, there is no place that pleasantly unifies the best of it and, especially for beginners, provides an easy way to enter the world of competitions without getting lost.
story.text2: The MathComps project was born with the goal of changing this state – to create a single place for the entire community where everything needed will be: a clear archive of problems, study materials, discussions on problems and competitions, personalized learning, and more; the imagination has no limits.
story.text3: The current version required a lot of time and full-time dedication, which would not have been possible without the support of our main sponsor, the company <link>Wincent</link>.
story.text4: Founded by former extremely successful participants of the Mathematical Olympiad, it has a very close relationship with the ideas of comprehensive support for the development of mathematical talents. Great thanks belong to them.
story.title: Why MathComps was created

competitions.description: The most important competition is the Mathematical Olympiad (MO). However, there are plenty of other competitions and activities that are good as training for MO or even on their own 😇.

howToStart.description: At the beginning, there are always many options on how to start. Then there are many options on how to progress. The following advice aims to help with this process.

finalNote.text: The key is to enjoy the process. The world of competitions and seminars attracts many people, and it can change the life of each of them for the better 😊
finalNote.title: In conclusion

mathOlympiad.categoriesOutro: , each with its own grade levels and rounds.
mathOlympiad.description: The Mathematical Olympiad is a competition in solving interesting problems, open to elementary and high schoolers alike, with an emphasis on justifying your reasoning. Each year it starts with a home round and builds up to the most prestigious international contest of all,

elementaryCategories.point1: Z5 – Z9 by elementary school grades (and corresponding grades of eight-year gymnasiums)
elementaryCategories.point2: Home and district rounds in each category
elementaryCategories.point3: In category Z9, also a regional and national round
elementaryCategories.title: Elementary categories

highSchoolCategories.point1: C for 1st, B for 2nd, A for 3rd and 4th year (and corresponding grades of eight-year gymnasiums)
highSchoolCategories.point2: Home, school, and regional rounds in each category
highSchoolCategories.point3: In category A, also a national round, from which you advance to a selection camp for international competitions
highSchoolCategories.selectionNote: Both countries have different rules for advancement, in Slovakia there's also a qualification needed, see the competition website
highSchoolCategories.title: High school categories

features: Week-long events with two days of math and the rest of the days full of trips and fun 🎉
The host country usually rotates, so you get to travel to many interesting places ✈️
A chance to meet people from all over the world who are just as into it 🤝
international.hint: Below are the ones Slovakia and Czechia take part in, details on clicking a card.
international.intro: The biggest draw is the international competitions.

mathOlympiad.sharedTasks: Czechia and Slovakia have shared problems but separate organizations:
mathOlympiad.tip: Don't be afraid to try solving higher categories, problems often don't require more complex knowledge and categories overlap. The best of the best often solved higher categories too.

otherCompetitions.description: Besides the olympiad and seminars, there are many other competitions, both team and individual, in all sorts of formats, mostly one-day, fun, laid-back events 😌

resources.description: A brief list of the most important study/community resources that are definitely worth knowing.

tips.ai: We all see that AI is getting better at math. It can be a quick helper when learning new things. Just be careful, as it's not always right and can make things up 🙃

seminars.description: Correspondence seminars are an integral part of Czech-Slovak mathematical culture.
features: Solving problems at home and sending solutions by mail (hence the name), although now mostly online ✉️
Several series of problems during the year 📝
Camps packed with fun and math as an essential part of them 🏕️
seminars.tip: Many people solve multiple seminars at the same time, both at elementary and high school level. It's also common for Slovaks to solve Czech seminars and vice versa. It's no coincidence that there's a big overlap between the best MO and seminar solvers 😉

whyCompetitions.description: Math competitions are not just about competition and math 🙂.
